page.layout: One column of italic verse, stanzas set in full lines; the page number and running head at the top; the catchword "Præfens" at the lower right.

p.i: Mutet tristitiam lætitiâ polus? Extinctum merito funere Guisium Cœli qui sobolem perdere voverat Plutoni Stygio, syderei chori Gaudent: syderibus se comitem ferat Aër, terra parens, humida corpora, Et quodcunque locis spirat in omnibus. At tu, præ reliquis, sancta Dei cohors, Ter defuncta malis, monstra quot unico Celabat varius pectore Guisius, Laudes pange Deo: qui Sisaram malum Salmunam, Iabin, Og, cum Seono Zebum, Extincto Guisio sustulit unico.

Hanc Hydram secuit pestiferam potens Alcides, genitum lumine quem patre Humanoq; fatum feminæ credimus, Illo tempore, quo carne Deum pij Natum concelebrant: debuit is mori Christum qui vetuit nasci: o Deus, Nostris pectoribus nascere: vividam Expromens solito more potentiam, Qua fulcire velis numine qui tuo Nixi, perpetuis expositi malis Durant, terra licet deneget his opem.
Contra turbinibus corripe feruidis Regni septa tui perdita qui volunt, Et lucem iubaris pellere splendidam.

page.notes: Ornamental marks (dingbats or fleurons) stand before "Mutet", "Aër", "Et" and "Alcides" and before the line "Sic HENRICE"; they are not transcribed as text. "HENRICE" is set in small capitals; "Sic" appears roman. The word "secuit" is read from a long s and could be "fecuit"; I have read it as secuit. "Humanoq;" has a q-with-tail abbreviation for -que, kept as printed. The long s has been rendered as a plain s throughout. The word "Præfens" at the lower right is the catchword for the next page.
